forces.title: Strong growth in paid subscriptions for streaming services
forces.description: Paid subscriptions for OTT platforms are projected to grow by nearly 30% over the next two years. This trend, coupled with SVOD segment revenues crossing US$1 billion in 2024 and expected to reach US$2.68 billion by 2030, indicates increasing consumer willingness to pay for premium content, securing a robust revenue stream for platforms.

forces.title: Digital platforms driving M&E sector's exponential growth and monetization
forces.description: Digital platforms, including OTT, are identified as the primary drivers of exponential growth and transformation in the Media & Entertainment sector. They are unlocking new monetization avenues through digital advertising, e-commerce campaigns, and rapidly growing paid subscriptions across video and music, cementing their central role in the industry's future and audience engagement.

forces.title: Increasing digital advertising spend drives AVOD growth
forces.description: Digital advertising is seeing substantial growth, accounting for nearly 46% of total ad spend in FY25 and projected to lead the M&E sector's growth. This surge directly benefits Advertising-based Video-On-Demand (AVOD) platforms, which saw revenues increase to US$ 3.25 billion in 2024 and are projected to reach US$ 6.48 billion by 2030.

forces.title: Growth of consumer-creator trend and user-generated content
forces.description: The rise of digital self-expression and the consumer-creator trend presents an opportunity for streaming platforms to engage users more deeply. By providing tools for content creation, sharing, and discussion, platforms can strengthen their competitive position, foster community, and potentially generate new forms of engaging, user-generated content, expanding their content library and appeal.

forces.title: Shifting intellectual property ownership models for content
forces.description: Revenue models for content production houses are changing, with a trend towards more co-owned or shared Intellectual Property (IP) between producers and platforms. This structural shift impacts how streaming platforms acquire and monetize content, potentially leading to deeper collaborations, shared risks, and evolving financial arrangements beyond traditional licensing, fostering long-term content partnerships.

forces.title: Higher long-term interest rates increase cost of capital
forces.description: Globally, persistent inflation, sovereign borrowing, and volatile capital flows are keeping long-term interest rates high, a trend unlikely to abate in the near future. This means a higher cost of capital for businesses, including OTT platforms, affecting their ability to secure funding for content investments, technological upgrades, and market expansion, potentially slowing growth or increasing financial burdens.

forces.title: Rising demand for regional language content on OTT platforms
forces.description: The share of regional languages in OTT content has significantly increased from 27% in 2020 to 56% in 2025. This growing preference for local, culturally rooted stories is a major growth driver, expanding the audience base and engagement for streaming services across India, particularly in non-Hindi speaking regions.

forces.title: High smartphone penetration and affordable data access
forces.description: Growing mobile and smartphone penetration, alongside affordable data access, significantly boosts online video viewing and OTT audience expansion. India's broadband internet subscribers exceeded 995.63 crore by September 2025, providing a vast and accessible consumer base for streaming services, particularly AVOD platforms, driving continued digital consumption growth.

forces.title: Government support for M&E content creation and export
forces.description: Government initiatives, such as setting up the National Centre of Excellence for Animation, Gaming, Visual Effects and Comics industry, and plans to increase M&E exports to US$ 10 billion by 2027, foster a supportive environment. This creates a larger pool of talent and content, which can directly benefit OTT platforms seeking diverse and high-quality local productions.

forces.title: Indian OTT tech capabilities offer global replication opportunities
forces.description: India has developed advanced online entertainment platforms notable for their complexity in search, recommendations, dubbing, subtitling, and managing high concurrent usage during sporting events. This expertise creates an opportunity for Indian companies to replicate and export these M&E app development and operational capabilities on a global scale, particularly in developing and maintaining streaming services.

forces.title: Rationalization of sports media rights due to monetization realities
forces.description: With the potential exception of the IPL, sports media rights are expected to rationalize in the near term, reflecting evolving monetization realities. This poses a key risk for streaming platforms heavily reliant on sports content to drive subscriptions and engagement, potentially impacting content acquisition costs and the ability to secure exclusive, high-value live sports programming.

forces.title: Migration from Linear TV to Connected TV and digital subscriptions
forces.description: The Media & Entertainment sector is experiencing a structural shift where consumers are transitioning from traditional Linear TV to Connected TV (CTV) and digital subscriptions. Linear Pay TV subscriptions are expected to decline, with digital subscriptions making up the lost ground. Weekly active CTV homes increased to 40 million in 2025, driving demand for OTT content.

forces.title: Differentiation in streaming strategy attracts specific audiences
forces.description: A focused and differentiated streaming strategy, such as Sony Pictures' Crunchyroll specializing in anime, allows platforms to cater to niche but growing categories. This approach helps to stand out in a competitive market and build a loyal subscriber base by serving specific content preferences, as opposed to broad general entertainment offerings.

forces.title: Content production investment rationalization by studios
forces.description: Indian studios rationalized content spend in 2025, reducing investment in high-cost premium OTT content and prime-time TV fiction. While budgets for tentpole films and reality shows remained stable, this indicates a shift towards more targeted content investments. OTT platforms may face altered content supply dynamics, potentially requiring more strategic partnerships or a focus on cost-efficient productions.

forces.title: Generative AI poses disruptive threat to content DSPs
forces.description: The advancement of agentic AI presents a disruptive and potentially existential threat to traditional Digital Service Providers (DSPs), including video OTT platforms. If content rightsholders bypass DSPs to strike deals directly with AI companies or new AI-native DSPs emerge, it could fragment content distribution and challenge existing revenue models, necessitating strategic adaptation from incumbents.

viewpoints.title: Differentiated streaming strategy crucial for navigating market disruption
viewpoints.description: Ravi Ahuja, CEO of Sony Pictures, emphasizes that a differentiated streaming strategy is vital in a disrupted media landscape. He highlights Sony Pictures' focus on being the only large independent studio without a general entertainment platform, allowing content-centric distribution. Their anime streaming service, Crunchyroll, is cited as a successful example of a differentiated and growing niche.

viewpoints.title: India's online video industry set for strong expansion by 2030
viewpoints.description: IBEF projects India's online video industry to grow significantly from US$ 4.31 billion in 2024 to US$ 9.17 billion by 2030. This robust expansion reflects increasing digital consumption across the country. The subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) segment is also expected to more than double within this period.

viewpoints.title: OTT segment poised for remarkable growth with subscription dominance
viewpoints.description: The OTT segment in India is expected to achieve a remarkable CAGR of 14.1%, reaching Rs. 21,032 crore (US$ 2.55 billion) by 2026. This growth is largely driven by subscription services, which are projected to account for 95% of total OTT revenue by 2026, up from 90.5% in 2021, indicating a strong trend towards paid content.

viewpoints.title: Indian OTT audience experiences continued expansion and strong penetration
viewpoints.description: The Ormax OTT Audience Report 2025 indicates substantial growth in India’s OTT audience, which increased by 9.9% year-on-year to 601.2 million users. Penetration reached 41%, primarily fueled by AVOD platforms, rising smartphone usage, and increasingly affordable data access, showcasing a continued surge in digital video consumption nationwide.
viewpoints.source_firm: Ormax OTT Audience Report 2025 (cited by IBEF)

viewpoints.title: India's OTT market surpasses INR272 billion, driven by regional content
viewpoints.description: Allu Aravind, Chairman of Geetha Arts and Founder of Aha, confirms India’s OTT market exceeded INR272 billion in 2025, with digital media now leading the M&E industry. A key driver is the significant rise of regional languages, whose share in OTT content surged from 27% in 2020 to 56% in 2025, proving that local stories travel furthest.

viewpoints.title: M&E sector is essential for escapism and digital self-expression
viewpoints.description: Ashish Pherwani, M&E Sector Leader at EY India, articulates that media and entertainment are no longer discretionary but essential frameworks for interpreting the world, finding relief, and self-expression. Audiences seek 'escapism' through immersive experiences like cinema, gaming, music, and short-form content, and engage in 'digital self-expression' as creators, driving profound shifts in the ecosystem.

viewpoints.title: Digital subscriptions compensate for declining Linear TV revenues
viewpoints.description: EY's analysis suggests that the decline in Linear TV subscriptions and associated revenues will be effectively offset by growth in digital subscriptions. This indicates a significant consumer migration from traditional broadcast to digital streaming platforms, underscoring the increasing importance and revenue-generating potential of OTT services in the Indian market.

viewpoints.title: D2C platforms continue investing in sports rights despite rationalization
viewpoints.description: EY notes that while sports media rights may rationalize (excluding IPL) due to monetization realities, large Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) platforms are expected to continue investing in cricket and other sports rights. This strategic investment aims to boost subscription revenues, enhance in-app engagement, and build customer loyalty, indicating sustained competition for premium content.

viewpoints.title: Paid subscriptions in OTT expected to grow nearly 30% in two years
viewpoints.description: Allu Aravind highlights that paid subscriptions for OTT content are projected to grow by almost 30% over the next two years. This signifies a strong consumer willingness to pay for quality content and underscores the increasing viability of subscription-based revenue models in the Indian streaming market, crucial for industry investment.

viewpoints.title: Digital subscription revenue to expand to 191 million households
viewpoints.description: EY projects significant growth in digital subscription revenue, anticipating an INR85 billion increase as video OTT subscriptions expand from 143 million households in 2025 to approximately 191 million by 2028. This upward trend underscores the rising adoption and willingness of Indian consumers to pay for digital video content.

viewpoints.title: Indian OTT tech capabilities offer global replication opportunities
viewpoints.description: EY identifies a significant opportunity for Indian OTT platforms, noting their development of some of the world's largest online entertainment platforms. These platforms excel in content complexities like search, recommendations, dubbing, and subtitling, as well as managing concurrent usage during major events, suggesting a potential for global replication and export of M&E app development expertise.

viewpoints.title: Digital platforms are central to M&E's exponential growth and monetization
viewpoints.description: Kevin Vaz, Chairman of the FICCI M&E Committee, states that digital platforms are fueling exponential growth and transforming revenue models within the Media & Entertainment sector. Rapidly growing paid subscriptions across video and music, alongside digital advertising, are unlocking new monetization avenues, cementing digital's pivotal role in the industry's future trajectory and audience engagement.

viewpoints.title: New media to dominate M&E revenues, comprising 53% by 2028
viewpoints.description: EY forecasts that 'new media,' encompassing digital media and video games, will become the predominant revenue source in the overall Media & Entertainment sector, projected to constitute 53% of total revenues by 2028. This shift highlights the growing influence and financial contribution of digital entertainment formats, including streaming services, within the industry.

viewpoints.title: AI to enhance content production efficiency, driving cost differentiation
viewpoints.description: EY anticipates that artificial intelligence will significantly improve production efficiencies in content creation for the Media & Entertainment sector. This technological advancement is expected to enable production houses to achieve cost differentiation, streamlining workflows and potentially leading to more cost-effective content for streaming platforms, thus enhancing profitability and competitive advantage.
